name: Turn The Tide: Short Seas (revised)
summary: Over P deals of 10 hands, players play Weather cards at the same time to dodge high Tide levels and keep their lifelines. Each deal the hands pass to the left, and the highest total score wins.

player.meaning: Game score summed over the deals.
Weather cards held and not yet played.
Weather cards this player has played face up in the current deal.
Weather card played in the current hand.
The 11 cards gathered for passing to the left at the start of a deal.

game.meaning: Shuffled Weather deck used for dealing.
The P Weather cards set aside unseen for the whole game.
Tide deck, refilled at the start of each deal.
Smaller of the two Tide cards revealed this hand.
Larger of the two Tide cards revealed this hand.
Current hand within the deal, from 1 to 10.
Scratch value: highest Tide level among non-Sunk players.
Scratch value: lowest Tide level among non-Sunk players at the end of a deal.

setup: Let P be the number of players (3 or 4).
weather_deck is set to the cards 1 to 12*P, each number once.
Each player draws 11 cards at random from weather_deck into hand, and each card is removed from weather_deck.
The remaining P cards move from weather_deck to set_aside, which is never shown.
Every score is 0, deal_no is 1 and hand_no is 1.

round.effect: When hand_no == 1 and deal_no >= 2: each player's pass_buffer = played + hand; then each player's hand = pass_buffer of the player on their right (each player passes to the left); played = [] for everyone.
When hand_no == 1: tide_deck = cards 1 to 20; every tide = 15; every lifelines = 4; every sunk = false.
When hand_no == 1, each player is sent their hand, along with deal_no and all public attributes.
Draw 2 cards at random from tide_deck and remove them from it; low_tide = the smaller, high_tide = the larger.
Announce: 'Deal {deal_no}, hand {hand_no}: Low Tide {low_tide}, High Tide {high_tide}.'
Each player's card_played = the chosen card; it is removed from hand and appended to played. All are revealed together.
The player with the highest card_played sets tide = low_tide. The player with the second-highest card_played sets tide = high_tide. Sunk players are included. Everyone else keeps their tide.

max_tide = the highest tide among players with sunk == false. For each player with sunk == false and tide == max_tide: if lifelines == 0 then sunk = true, else lifelines -= 1. If every player is Sunk, nothing changes.
Announce every card_played, tide, lifelines and sunk.

When hand_no == 10: each player with sunk == false adds lifelines to score; each player with sunk == true subtracts 1 from score; min_tide = the lowest tide among players with sunk == false; each player with sunk == false and tide == min_tide adds 1 to score.
hand_no += 1; if hand_no > 10 then hand_no = 1 and deal_no += 1.
End the game when deal_no > P; otherwise continue.

ending.decided_by: The highest game score wins. A tie is broken by the lowest Tide level at the end of the last deal. Players still level on both share the win, which stands in for the source's draw.

rules.text: At setup, the Weather deck is the cards 1 to 12*P, each player is dealt 11 cards into hand, and the remaining P cards go to set_aside and are never shown.
At the start of every deal, tide_deck is reset to 1 to 20, every tide is 15, every lifelines is 4 and every sunk is false.
At the start of deals 2 to P, each player's played cards plus their 1 remaining card (11 cards) pass to the player on their left as that player's hand, and played becomes empty.
Each hand, two Tide cards are drawn from tide_deck; the smaller is low_tide and the larger is high_tide.
Each hand, every player chooses one card from hand at the same time; it is removed from hand, appended to played and revealed.
The player who played the highest Weather card sets tide = low_tide, and the player who played the second highest sets tide = high_tide; this includes Sunk players.
Every non-Sunk player whose tide equals the highest tide among non-Sunk players loses 1 lifeline; a player at 0 lifelines who must lose one becomes Sunk instead.
A Sunk player stays Sunk until the next deal, still plays cards and is ignored when lifelines are lost; if all players are Sunk, no lifelines are lost.
After hand 10 of a deal, each non-Sunk player adds their lifelines (0 to 4) to score.
After hand 10 of a deal, each Sunk player subtracts 1 from score.
After hand 10 of a deal, each non-Sunk player whose tide is the lowest among non-Sunk players adds 1 to score.
A deal has 10 hands and the game ends after deal P.
The highest score wins; a tie is broken by the lowest final tide; players still level share the win.

offers.question: Choose a Weather card to play this hand
offers.options: Exactly the cards currently in that seat's hand: 11 options on hand 1 of a deal, down to 2 on hand 10.

choices.why: The designer suggests 4, and the deck size and deal count scale with P. With fewer than 3 players, the highest and second-highest cards decide everyone's Tide. More than 4 is outside the deck design.
The rules state there is no talk phase.
Tide is between 1 and 20, so it never outweighs a point of score, and a lower tide ranks higher.

choices.what: Hand passing modelled with a pass_buffer list
choices.why: All players pass at once, so each 11-card set is gathered first and then moved to the left-hand neighbour.

choices.what: Count-dependent numbers written per player (weather_cards_per_player 12, deals_per_player 1, set_aside_cards_per_player 1)
choices.why: Parameters must be plain numbers. The Weather deck is 12*P cards, there are 1*P deals and 1*P cards set aside, so each holds at 3 and at 4 players.

simplifications.what: The source's draw becomes a shared win
simplifications.why: The engine has no separate draw: players level at the top share the win.

simplifications.what: Start-of-deal and end-of-deal work is done by steps conditioned on hand_no
simplifications.why: The step list is flat, so these steps run every round but act only on hand 1 or hand 10.
